**All Out (2021)** was a major professional wrestling pay-per-view (PPV) event produced by **All Elite Wrestling (AEW)**—and it’s widely remembered as one of AEW’s most significant shows due to its match quality and multiple landmark moments.

---

## Core details
- **Event name:** All Out (2021)  
- **Promotion:** All Elite Wrestling (AEW)  
- **Date:** **September 5, 2021**  
- **Venue:** **Now Arena**  
- **City:** **Hoffman Estates, Illinois** (Chicago metro area)  
- **Broadcast:** Traditional PPV and streaming platforms (varied by region)  
- **Branding/identity:** Part of AEW’s annual “All Out” series (one of the company’s signature PPVs)

---

## Why it’s historically important
All Out 2021 is often cited as a turning-point AEW show because it combined:
- **A very strong in-ring card**
- **Major roster additions revealed on the show**
- **A huge “Chicago” atmosphere**, tied to several performers’ connections to the city

Most notably, the event featured:
- **CM Punk’s first major singles match in over 7 years**
- **Major post-main-event debuts** (and one surprise during the show)

---

## Main card results (in show order, commonly listed)
**AEW TNT Championship**
- **Miro (c) def. Eddie Kingston**  
  (Hard-hitting, physical title match.)

**AEW Women’s World Championship**
- **Dr. Britt Baker, D.M.D. (c) def. Kris Statlander**  
  (Baker retained in a high-profile women’s title defense.)

**AEW World Tag Team Championship – Steel Cage**
- **The Young Bucks (c) def. The Lucha Bros (Penta El Zero Miedo & Rey Fénix)**  
  (Lucha Bros won the match and the titles; this is widely regarded as a classic and one of the defining matches of AEW’s early era.)

**Casino Battle Royale (winner earns a future title shot)**
- **Ruby Soho won**  
  Notable because **Ruby Soho (formerly Ruby Riott in WWE)** debuted as the “Joker” entrant and won immediately.

**Jon Moxley def. Satoshi Kojima**
- A special attraction match featuring Japanese wrestling legend **Satoshi Kojima**.

**AEW World Championship**
- **Kenny Omega (c) def. Christian Cage**  
  Omega retained the world title.

**CM Punk def. Darby Allin**
- Punk’s long-awaited in-ring return in a major singles match; a centerpiece attraction of the show.

**Paul Wight def. QT Marshall**
- A short “special attraction” style match featuring the former Big Show.

**Chris Jericho def. MJF**
- A major grudge match; Jericho won, concluding the feud’s PPV arc.

---

## Major debuts and surprise moments
All Out 2021 is especially famous for what happened *around* the main event:

### Ruby Soho
- Debuted in the **Casino Battle Royale** as the surprise “Joker” entrant and **won**.

### Adam Cole
- **Debuted after the main event**, confronting key players and aligning himself with **The Elite**, which was a huge moment given his prominence elsewhere before AEW.

### Bryan Danielson
- **Debuted moments after Adam Cole**, creating an immediate top-tier “new era” feeling and setting up major future matches and stories.

These consecutive debuts (especially **Cole** and **Danielson** back-to-back) made the show feel unusually newsworthy even by big-PPV standards.

---

## Reception and legacy
- The event is frequently praised for:
  - The **Young Bucks vs. Lucha Bros steel cage** match (often singled out as match-of-the-night and one of AEW’s best ever)
  - The crowd energy (Chicago-area audience)
  - The “stacked” feeling of the show—big matches plus major surprises
- All Out 2021 is commonly discussed as one of AEW’s strongest PPVs, alongside other highly regarded AEW tentpole events.

---

## Business/impact notes (high level)
- It’s widely reported and discussed as one of AEW’s **strongest-performing PPVs** up to that point, buoyed by:
  - CM Punk’s return run
  - Heavy anticipation for surprises
  - A card loaded with title matches and grudge matches

---
